title: Security vendor ships ML deserialization scanning as a named tier by Q1 2027
body: By Q1 2027 at least one named application-security or supply-chain-security platform (the Snyk / Endor Labs / JFrog / Protect AI / HiddenLayer class of vendors) will market a productized, named capability that scans the machine-learning data-and-metadata plane for unsafe-deserialization and untrusted-serialized-object risk — pickle/dill/joblib payloads, model checkpoints, and feature-store transformation bodies — as a first-class scanner tier, not a buried CVE-feed entry. Feast's June 24 CVE-2026-56121 is the structural trigger: a maximum-severity (CVSS 9.3 v4.0) unauthenticated RCE in which the registry server base64-decodes a user-supplied feature-view function body and hands it straight to dill.loads() before any authorization check, proving the attack surface has moved one layer below the model and inference engine into the ML plumbing that ingests serialized logic over the network. That is the same unsafe-deserialization primitive OWASP's agentic-AI work and the broader CVE drumbeat keep surfacing, and once a class of bug has both a documented exploit trail and a network-reachable, weaponizable shape, security vendors productize a dedicated detection surface for it rather than leaving it to generic dependency scanning. The falsifiable core is a NAMED, marketed product tier, module, or SKU whose stated scope explicitly covers ML serialized-artifact / deserialization / model-supply-chain scanning — announced in vendor docs, a release, or a launch. What does NOT count: a generic SCA tool merely ingesting the Feast CVE into its existing vulnerability feed, a one-off blog post or advisory, an internal research demo, or a prompt-injection / agent-runtime guardrail product (that is a different attack class). The deeper read is that zero-trust treatment of serialized ML artifacts — signing, provenance, and gated deserialization — becomes a sellable layer, but the load-bearing checkable claim is the named scanning tier.

reasoning.because: Feast CVE-2026-56121: unauthenticated CVSS-9.3 RCE; registry dill.loads() a user body pre-auth
reasoning.given: The ML attack surface dropped into the serialized data plane; the deserialization-RCE pattern recurs
reasoning.so_that: A named security vendor ships ML deserialization scanning as a marketed product tier, not a CVE-feed entry
reasoning.landing: by Q1 2027; one named vendor tier/SKU covering ML deserialization scanning
reasoning.plain_language: A critical AI-data bug let attackers run code via a booby-trapped file, so a security company will sell a scanner to catch that.

summary: Feast's June 24 CVE-2026-56121 is an unauthenticated CVSS-9.3 RCE: the registry runs dill.loads() on a user-supplied body, showing the ML attack surface dropped into the serialized data plane. Expect a named security vendor to ship ML deserialization scanning as a marketed product tier by Q1 2027.
